newsitem.title: UK: UK refers Nat Express deals to monopoly body.
newsitem.headline: UK refers Nat Express deals to monopoly body.

text.p: The British government on Thursday said it is referring to the Monopolies and Mergers Commission (MMC) National Express Group Plc's planned purchase of the regional Scotrail rail network.

Margaret Beckett, president of the Board of Trade also announced her decision to refer National Express' acquisition of the Central Trains Ltd rail franchise in the West Midlands to the MMC for investigation.

"I consider that the acquisition by National Express of ScotRail raises competition concerns in the market for the supply of public transport passenger services in Scotland," Margaret Beckett, Secretary of State for Trade and Industry, said in a statement.

"Separately, I consider that the acquisition by National Express of Central Trains raises competition concerns in the supply of public transport services in the West Midlands region (of England)," she added.
The MMC are required to make their reports by September 19, this year.
Beckett said the two decisions do not prejudge the question of whether the acquisitions are against the public interest -- it is for the MMC to decide on that after their investigations.
Shares in National Express dropped to 492 pence on the news, down 27 pence and compared with around 514 pence before the announcement.
